udp_state_lifetime_review.finding: The application UDP echo server retains its states map for the process lifetime, keyed only by remote source address. State base advances after each full 32-datagram window and no completed-flow deletion, per-transfer reset, unique transfer ID, or expiry is present. If a later flow reuses that source endpoint, sequence 0 is compared against the prior nonzero base and causes unexpected UDP window.
udp_state_lifetime_review.coverage_gap: The v2 reorder/duplicate controls each start a separate echo-server process; they do not exercise a second transfer or source-address reuse against the same server. The actual runner starts one echo server for the entire cell loop.
udp_state_lifetime_review.smoke_observation: The v2 smoke archive records 5/40 cells then failure at ssclassic-freedom/UDP/official after about 60 seconds. Echo log contains only READY and the sample records a client UDP read timeout; evidence does not establish that stale state caused this specific failure.
udp_state_lifetime_review.required_before_udp_timing: Apply explicit transfer-start/ack that resets state before data and starts timing at first data, or scope state by a unique transfer ID; add a bounded consecutive-transfer/source-reuse control on one server and retain reorder/duplicate controls. Before another attempt at the failed UDP smoke, capture stage/datagram evidence distinguishing first-burst data loss, ACK delivery, and route setup; timeout plus READY-only echo log proves neither stale-port reuse nor the timeout cause. Preserve both failed UDP smoke archives unchanged.
udp_state_lifetime_review.scope_note: These UDP diagnosis/fix checks do not globally block independent TCP-chain proof or preparation. No full performance measurements were run by this auditor.
udp_state_lifetime_review.status: Confirmed source-level lifecycle hazard; specific smoke failure cause unconfirmed; no timing run or raw performance audit.
